numerical_failure.observed_behavior: The nnls inner loop uses the constraint check s[P].min() <= tol (tolerance-based) instead of s[P].min() <= 0, causing non-converging iterations on well-posed problems; with MKL/AVX512 BLAS, TestNNLS.test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 fails with RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The constraint violation check should be s[P].min() <= 0 per the referenced algorithm paper, so the iteration converges for well-posed problems and test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 passes.
trigger_conditions: nnls solver inner loop constraint check on s[P] using tolerance
MKL-flavour BLAS/LAPACK with AVX512 instructions (per issue #20470)
well-posed problems such as TestNNLS.test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 where the iteration fails to converge
adding k = k + 1e-10 * np.random.normal(size=N) to the test input makes the test pass (reported workaround)

input_output_examples.input: nnls(W @ A, W @ k) in TestNNLS.test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 (MKL build with AVX512)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached.

oracle_clues: test_nnls_max_iterations regression test added in PR#20168 discussion
paper-based reference: constraint should be s[P].min() <= 0
maintainer note that exact zeros are not feasible in floating point so a tolerance is normally used, questioned whether it causes errors

numerical_characteristics.tolerance: The original check used s[P].min() <= tol with a tiny tolerance (1e-10 perturbation referenced in tests); the fix changes the check to s[P].min() <= 0 per the cited paper; test asserts assert_allclose with rtol=0 and atol=1e-10
category_specific_evidence: The bug was an infinite loop / non-converging iterations in the inner loop of the nnls solver (scipy/optimize/_nnls.py), reported as 'Maximum number of iterations reached.'
Original constraint check s[P].min() <= tol was wrong; the paper-based correct check is s[P].min() <= 0 (PR#20168)
Tiny tolerance was used to avoid an infinite loop; maintainers note hitting exact zeros is not feasible in floating point so a tol is used to treat small values as zero
Small perturbations such as k = k + 1e-10 * np.random.normal(size=N) make the infinite loop go away, and the issue author asked to increase the 1e-10 value until the problem disappears
Behaviour is possibly sensitive to SIMD instruction set, as noted in issue#20470
Regression test test_nnls_inner_loop_case2 uses a specific input vector n and k from gh-20168 and checks nnls(W @ A, W @ k) against expected d with assert_allclose(rtol=0., atol=1e-10)

provenance.value: The nnls inner loop uses the constraint check s[P].min() <= tol (tolerance-based) instead of s[P].min() <= 0, causing non-converging iterations on well-posed problems; with MKL/AVX512 BLAS, TestNNLS.test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 fails with RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached.
The constraint violation check should be s[P].min() <= 0 per the referenced algorithm paper, so the iteration converges for well-posed problems and test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 passes.

The original check used s[P].min() <= tol with a tiny tolerance (1e-10 perturbation referenced in tests); the fix changes the check to s[P].min() <= 0 per the cited paper; test asserts assert_allclose with rtol=0 and atol=1e-10
